name: @kanzo-tech/mosaic
description: The Mosaic conversation, without React — coordinator, clients and clauses re-exported as one surface, plus the Arrow column reader and the page's one DuckDB-WASM engine.

scripts.build: node scripts/extensions.mjs && rm -rf dist && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json

//dependencies: @duckdb/duckdb-wasm is a dependency, exact, not a peer. `engine()` names its worker and module as `new URL("@duckdb/duckdb-wasm/dist/…", import.meta.url)` — the spelling DuckDB-WASM documents for webpack — so the host's bundler emits them from this package's own copy, and they must be the release the JavaScript driving them comes from and the one the pinned httpfs was built for. A range, or a peer the host resolves, would let the three drift. It is also the release mosaic-core pins, so the tree holds one copy; `scripts/extensions.test.mjs` fails when either moves.
//peers: mosaic-core and mosaic-sql are REQUIRED, not optional, and that is the whole point of this package: there is nothing here without them, so a host installs them once and both @kanzo-tech/ui/analytics and @kanzo-tech/graph/duckdb see the same coordinator. Two copies would be two crossfilters. @uwdata/vgplot is deliberately absent — it is a plotting library, it belongs to the charts in @kanzo-tech/ui, and its accidental presence on this path is exactly the bug this package exists to end. Both ranges are ^0.32.0, the floor where a failed query reaches a client as mosaic-core's `QueryError` wrapping what DuckDB threw — `queryFailure` (src/failure.ts) unwraps it at every client in @kanzo-tech/ui and @kanzo-tech/graph, so the floor is load-bearing. 0.29 also published a `workspace:^` peer range that npm cannot install. Each range names the newest release that exists; raise both together.
//build: tsc, not Vite, and the reason is the `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` lines of src/engine.ts. Those expressions have to reach the HOST's bundler verbatim, which is what makes DuckDB's worker, module and httpfs assets of the host's page. Vite's library mode inlines every asset it resolves, and it resolved the extension into a 1,088 kB engine.js of base64; `?no-inline` emitted it instead, but under a root-absolute URL and renamed `httpfs2.…`, and DuckDB looks up an extension's entrypoint by the file name's first segment. Nothing here needed Vite: no JSX, no CSS, no directive, and nothing to bundle, since every import is a package the host resolves. `extensions/` sits beside `dist/` rather than inside it for the same line: `../extensions` resolves identically from `src/` and from `dist/`, so the test and the tarball read the same path.
